A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RGMem. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original RGMem evaluations on LOCOMO and PersonaMem, component ablations, parameter sensitivity, and profile-convergence results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds targeted ablations, update-strategy comparisons, injected preference-shift experiments, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The method equations, Algorithm 1, implementation defaults, and prompt templates are retained. The new discussion of fixed semantic anchors and the correction term explains and tests existing components; it does not establish a changed RGMem procedure.

E1.justification: LOCOMO and PersonaMem under the 128k setting remain the benchmarks. Appendix B.7 adds deliberately injected gradual preference changes and abrupt reversals after profile stabilization, extending the tested dialogue conditions.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. New appendix comparisons evaluate L0+GraphRAG using RGMem's extracted facts (Table 5), plus High-Frequency and Periodic Global Rewrite update strategies (Table 7).

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols use a 20% PersonaMem subset, compare update schedules including θinf=1, measure similarity to initial and final profiles under injected shifts, and account for end-to-end costs per session. The retained benchmark backbones, judging protocol, accuracy metrics, and default settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained layer ablations and sensitivity analyses, v3 tests semantic anchoring, removal of the correction term, and alternative update triggers (Tables 5–7). Figures 8–10 examine update stability and controlled preference shifts. Appendix B.9 analyzes operational overhead, while Appendix C adds an illustrative hallucination-isolation trace.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three runs with different random seeds and report averages. v3 adds no new uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their scores. New subset results include Latest Preference accuracy of 74.11% with correction-term extraction versus 52.58% without it (Table 6), and update-strategy accuracies of 65.32%, 53.72%, and 48.95% (Table 7). New trajectory and operational-cost results substantially expand the findings; these are additions, not performance gains over v2 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Proposition B.1 in v2 becomes D.1 in v3, with the Hoeffding error-bound exponent corrected from -2n(1-2ε)^2 to -n(1-2ε)^2/2 for observations in [-1,1]. The derivation is expanded accordingly; the proposition's conclusion and other propositions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same RG-inspired memory contribution, four motivating insights, benchmark-superiority claims, and stated improvement margins. The appendix additions support existing headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations linking semantic anchors to reduced drift, correction-term extraction to preserved conflicting preferences, and thresholded processing to controlled costs. Appendix C also introduces the categorical assertion that uncorroborated errors cannot contaminate higher abstractions or retrieval, extending the robustness interpretation beyond what its single illustrative trace establishes.

D1.justification: The added comparisons describe construction of the GraphRAG and summary/update variants, and Table 8 newly discloses whole-pipeline runtime, API-call counts, and input/output token totals. Existing implementation defaults, prompt templates, and the stated code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds He et al. (2026) on continual-learning subspaces, Chen et al. (2026) on MoE forgetting, and Zhu et al. (2026) on latent memory evolution. These modestly extend positioning against implicit memory; other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v3 expands the appendix contents guide, moves experimental material before theory, introduces ablation subheadings, standardizes proof-step labels, and updates affiliations and publication information. This is localized restructuring rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Tables 5–8 and Figures 8–10 substantially expand the visual presentation of mechanism comparisons, profile dynamics, and operational costs. Retained Figures 6–7 are regrouped into a compact row; the former Figure 8 becomes Figure 11. Figure 6 is restyled without changing its values, and Table 2 gains a stray 'icml2026 (2)' header.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects a mathematical bound and adds useful evidence isolating design choices and exposing total operational costs, addressing gaps in v2's bundled ablations and retrieval-token accounting. The gains are limited by underspecified subset selection and injected-dialogue construction, while Appendix C overgeneralizes an illustrative trace into an error-isolation guarantee. Overall, the revision provides a modest net improvement in evidential support and transparency.
